subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The River
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The River.

hook.text: The Buddha compared life to a river—always flowing, never the same twice. Heraclitus said the same.

buildup.text: Rivers mark boundaries. The Styx divides life and death. The Jordan divides old and new covenants.

discovery.text: In Hindu belief, bathing in the Ganges washes away sins. The river itself is a goddess named Ganga.

twist.text: Rivers also flood and destroy. Mesopotamia's flood myths began because the Tigris was unpredictable.

climax.text: A river is time made visible. It flows one way, carries everything, and cannot be reversed.

punchline.text: You can't step in the same one twice.

quiz.question: Which river separates the living from the dead in Greek myth?
